subject: E2E private deploy: egress onboarding + IP custody checkpoint
messages:
From: Andrew Collins <andrew.collins@acmehealth.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2028-03-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private endpoint onboarding: egress domains, IP custody

Hi Jasmine,

We're kicking off the private deployment for Acme Health (VPC/private runtime). Before we schedule the network handover window, we need a concise list of the exact networking requirements Redwood expects from our side for IP allowlisting, firewall rules, and egress controls. Specifically:

- Do you support pinned exit IPs for private endpoints or do you require a proxy/NAT on our side?
- If you provide static egress IPs, what level of SLA and rotation policy should we expect?
- For customers that prefer to proxy, what are recommended TLS/mTLS settings and FQDNs to allow?
- What audit evidence do you provide for SOC2/security reviews (logs, signed attestations, IP ownership proof)?

We're preparing the compliance bundle for our security team. If you can send a short checklist and example firewall snippet (FQDNs/ports/cidrs) we can map to our perimeter rules.

Target: staging handover week of 2028-03-20. Can we lock required items this week?

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Collins
SRE Manager, Acme Health
(andrew.collins@acmehealth.com)

Subject: Re: Private endpoint onboarding: egress domains, IP custody

Hi Andrew — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then next steps and an attachment.

- Pinned egress: For Redwood Private we offer two patterns: (1) pinned NAT egress IPs (recommended for strict allowlists), or (2) a customer-side egress proxy (recommended when customers maintain strict egress control and want full IP custody).
- Rotation: If you pick our pinned egress, IP rotation is configurable (we support rotation windows as short as 7 days for ephemeral pools or static assignment for the project lifetime).
- Proxy/mTLS: We recommend an upstream reverse-proxy with mTLS to our control plane if you need mutual authentication; we'll provide CA details and expected SNI/FQDNs.
- Evidence: We can provide a signed attestation, the egress IP manifest (CSV), per-request metadata in logs and a tarball of flow evidence for your audit team.

Next steps (this week):
1) See attached egress-onboarding-checklist.md — fill in the highlighted fields (preferred model for egress, staging CIDRs, SRE contact).
2) If you want pinned IPs, confirm whether you need single-static (one IP) or small CIDR (/29) for operator convenience.
3) Marissa will provide sample firewall rules and a permitlist template.

I'll hold a 30-min slot Thu 2028-03-08 16:00 ET to review the filled checklist — call details in the calendar invite.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Date: 2028-03-06T08:32:00Z
Subject: Firewall snippets + permitlist template for Acme Health staging

Andrew — attaching a short set of firewall snippets you can drop into perimeter rules plus a permitlist template. Key notes below.

Firewall snippets (summary):
- Control plane (required): allow outbound TCP 443 to control.redwood.ai (FQDN), SNI control.redwood.ai, IPs may be updated; allow by FQDN where possible.
- Runtime egress (optional static): if you choose Redwood pinned egress we will allocate either a single public IP or a /29. Allow outbound traffic from that IP to your collector endpoints.
- Proxy pattern: allow outbound to proxy.example.acmehealth.internal:443 and accept inbound from our health-check IP range during onboarding window.
- DNS: allow DNS egress to your resolvers; we recommend split-horizon to resolve internal FQDNs.

Suggested rule examples (permitlist-template.csv):
- Type,Protocol,Source,Dest,FQDN/Notes
- outbound,tcp,10.0.0.0/24,control.redwood.ai,443 (by SNI)
- outbound,tcp,10.0.0.0/24,34.201.55.12,443 (optional pinned egress)

Ephemeral IPs + rotation: If you elect ephemeral pools, we'll publish a rotation cadence and deliver the next-rotation manifest 48 hours before change. If your firewall cannot accept short notice rotations, choose the static assignment.

Attachments: firewall-snippets.md and permitlist-template.csv (CSV).

Let us know whether Acme needs us to present this to your Network/Compliance team — we can join the call.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Network Security Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Andrew — great questions. Confirming the bundle and next steps below.

Evidence bundle we will provide (egress-proof-bundle.zip):
- Signed egress custody attestation (PDF) — indicates whether Redwood or Acme holds IP custody.
- Egress IP manifest CSV (current assignment + rotation history).
- Sample per-request log (anonymized) showing timestamp, request-id, source (pod id), dest FQDN, SNI, and egress IP.
- Short README describing rotation cadence and how to validate logs against requests.

Rotation overlap: we support a configurable overlap window. For customers that need change-control overlap, we can enable a 7-day dual-announce grace period (both old and new IPs accepted). We'll log the overlap and include it in the manifest.

Pinned vs proxy decision guidance:
- If your firewall team cannot accept dynamic rotations, pick pinned static assignment (we recommend a /29 for operational headroom).
- If you need absolute IP custody and cannot rely on Redwood-assigned IPs, the proxy pattern (customer side) gives you full control; we'll support mTLS and provide CA certs and SNI allowlist.

Action items we need from Acme by 2028-03-10:
1) Fill and return egress-onboarding-checklist.md (preferred pattern, staging CIDRs, contact).
2) Sign the egress custody attestation via DocuSign (link in thread).
3) Confirm whether you want pinned /29 or proxy pattern for staging.

Scheduling: Once we have the filled checklist and attestation, we propose a 3-hour handover on 2028-03-21 10:00-13:00 ET for environment validation and test traffic. We'll bring Network + Security and a runtime engineer.

I'll attach the evidence bundle and hubspot link once the attestation is signed. If helpful, Rishi and Olga will join the compliance call.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
